mentl/00a5735:
Substrate-native answers to two Ω.4-prep questions:

Q1 — Token payload + Span. Token wraps as Tok(TokenKind, Span)
mirroring the existing N(NodeBody, Span, Int) pattern for AST
nodes. Same wrapper discipline at every layer; one Span field
stored once per token; uniform accessors (token_kind / token_span)
match the N-pattern accessors. Adding a TokenKind variant has zero
impact on the wrapper.

Q2 — Token enumeration completeness. SYNTAX.md pre-declares every
TokenKind variant; Ω.4's parser refactor implements against the
declared set. Same Σ → Ω.4 contract as the rest of the syntax
spec. H6's exhaustive-match discipline propagates: parser's match
on Token MUST cover every variant or fail to compile.

Enumeration: 69 variants total —
  • 24 keywords
  • 5 identifier+literals (TIdent / TInt / TFloat / TString /
    TDocComment, all carry payload)
  • 15 two-character operators (incl. all five pipe verbs)
  • 23 single-character operators and punctuation
  • 2 layout (TNewline, TEof)

Each variant gets a row in the catalog table: lexical form,
payload type, expected parse contexts. Lexer obligations
(exhaustive emit set, whitespace consumption, line vs doc
comment behavior) and parser obligations (exhaustive match,
span propagation, generic-bracket disambiguation, pipe-vs-or)
also specified.

Brainstormed via the substrate-first lens: the Node wrapper
pattern was already the answer for Q1. The Σ → Ω.4 discipline
was already the answer for Q2. Both extensions are existing
substrate shapes applied at the token layer. Neither requires
new mechanism.

Next: Ω.4 lands the parser refactor against this enumeration.
